payload_digest.description: SHA-256 address of the immutable payload, when accepted.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

PayloadFinding.description:
One finding in the merged payload report.

The battery over a [`Payload`] emits these; `PAY-1` emits the anchoring and
staleness families, and the remaining families (continuity, factcheck,
outline-conformance, craft, proof, naming, phase, lexicon) merge in here in
`PAY-2`. Every finding is fully attributed: the draft [`line`](Self::line) and
verbatim [`quote`](Self::quote) it turns on, the [`code`](Self::code) of the
rule or check that raised it, the [`principle`](Self::principle) it cites when
the check is craft, its supporting [`citations`](Self::citations), and the
[`grade`](Self::grade) of the evidence.

citations.description: Ledger citations backing the finding (`d-nnnn`), when it turns on a ruling.

code.description: The stable dotted class code (`family.item`), e.g. `anchor.quote-missing`.

grade.description:
The verification grade of the check that produced it. Every deterministic
kernel check re-derives exactly, so `PAY-1`'s findings carry
[`Grade::Checked`].

line.description: The draft line the finding turns on, when it anchors to one.

message.description: A domain-spoken description of the finding.

principle.description: The craft principle this finding cites, when the check is a craft rule.

quote.description: The verbatim quote from the draft the finding renders, when it has one.

severity.description: How much the finding must be attended to.

Severity.description: How much a [`WorldFinding`] must be attended to.

oneOf.description:
A violation: the world (or a draft) contradicts canon or asserts what it
may not.
A defect worth a look that does not, on its own, break canon.
